agent.problem: Stop 1 overuses unrevealed-detail guesses. Cards 2, 5, 7, 11, 14 and 17 do not provide enough earlier context to eliminate the alternatives, making six of the stop's ten choices discovery guesses rather than informed ones. Rework several setups or questions so only a few discoveries remain.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: The correct answer stands out visually: "Jesus" is a bare one-word answer, while both wrong answers are three-word descriptions, "The angel Gabriel" and "The prophet Elijah." Make the answers comparable in length and form.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

agent.problem: "While all this happens" depends on earlier cards without identifying what the men are reacting to. The question should briefly reestablish the light-and-voice encounter so it remains self-contained when the story card is no longer visible.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
